evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry reports the Shuowen form and gloss as “次也。从竹、弟” (sequence; from bamboo and 弟), and cites Duan Yucai's note that the popular form shortened 弟 in writing. It records senses including order/rank, ordinal use before numerals, examination rank, evaluation, passing an examination, and an elite residence. These are dictionary reports, not independent dated first attestations.
evidence.title: A02993 第 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: 說文解字注; 康熙字典; 音韻方言
evidence.text: The displayed Shuowen commentary says 第 means “sequence,” is written from 竹 and 弟, and quotes Duan's comment that the common form abbreviated 弟. The Kangxi entry gives Guangyun fanqie 特計切, glosses sequence, and separately records ‘only/just’ and residences; it also says 第 was originally written 弟. ZDIC reports modern Mandarin dì, Cantonese dai6, Tang-period *dhèi, and Middle Chinese 定母霽韻去聲 特計切. Its Old Chinese summary names Huang Kan and Wang Li systems but gives no reconstruction in the displayed passage.
evidence.title: 第 dì - 汉典

evidence.field: historical exemplification; entry citations
evidence.text: ZDIC cites 《小爾雅·廣詁》 for “第，次也,” 《釋名·釋書契》 for the claim that book titles use 第 because of sequence and that 竹 was added for book-related use, and 左傳·哀公十六年 for 楚國第. These sources establish dictionary-reported older attestations/interpretations, but the page does not supply manuscript dates or establish the precise historical semantic path. It separately quotes the Han Shu evaluation use ‘第其高下’ and Shi Ji ‘君第重射’ (‘just/only’), showing that ranking/evaluating and adverbial uses should not be collapsed into the graphic origin.
evidence.title: 第 dì - 汉典

evidence.field: 字源字形; archaeological form inventory
evidence.text: The entry lists seven oracle-bone examples, thirteen bronze examples, Chu manuscripts, Qin manuscripts, Shuowen small seal, and clerical forms. This supports the existence of a long graphic record, but the opened page exposes no actual glyph drawings or detailed graph-by-graph analysis in its text. No claim about what individual early forms depict or when a specific component was added can be established from this text alone.
evidence.title: 第 dì - 汉典

evidence.text: The database describes its resources as including archaic-script forms, component trees, etymological explanations, and Shuowen search; it credits paleographic materials for oracle-bone and bronze forms. The accessible home page did not provide a 第-specific analysis in this research session.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 / Multi-function Chinese Character Database

evidence.text: The inspected source page lists oracle, bronze, Chu manuscript, Qin manuscript, Shuowen seal and clerical script categories for 第 and cites 說文新證 among its reference works. Its graphic images were not visually inspected here, so this is only evidence that the page indexes those stages, not independent evidence for their visual interpretation.

evidence.text: The entry's metadata calls 第 pictographic, while its detailed explanation calls it a phono-semantic graph formed from 竹 and 弟聲. It also reports that 第 was originally written 弟 and quotes the Shuowen commentary that the common form shortened 弟. These are conflicting lexicographic accounts; neither establishes when the differentiated form arose.

The index alone does not establish their component shapes, chronology or whether a graph was corrupted.

evidence.field: 字源字形; cited texts and senses
evidence.text: ZDIC cites 《小爾雅·廣詁》 for 第，次也, 《釋名·釋書契》 for an explanation linking 第 and book sequence, and 《左傳·哀公十六年》 for 楚國第. evidence.field: 哀公十六年傳
evidence.text: The inspected transmitted text reads 楚國第 in a passage narrating events under Duke Ai's sixteenth year; its commentary glosses it as 用士之次第, ‘the order of employing officers’. This establishes the reading in this textual witness, not the date of the surviving manuscript or the graph's first use.
evidence.title: 春秋左傳正義/卷60

evidence.field: 廣詁
evidence.text: The inspected transcription reads 承、弟、班、列，次也, using 弟 rather than 第 in its sequence gloss. This differs from ZDIC's citation of 第，次也. The discrepancy may reflect textual or quotation differences; the inspected page does not establish which reading is earlier.
evidence.title: 《小尔雅》在线阅读

evidence.field: 王褒傳
evidence.text: The inspected text uses 第 in 第其高下, describing the ranking of performances. This supports an evaluation/ranking use in a Han historical text; it does not make that the graph's original sense.
evidence.title: 漢書/卷064下

evidence.field: 與元九書
evidence.text: The inspected text, dated 815 in its page context, uses 既第之后, referring to the time after passing an examination. This is a dated textual example of the examination-success sense, not evidence for the graph's origin.
evidence.title: 與元九書

evidence.field: Old Chinese and Middle Chinese readings; character formation
evidence.text: The entry reports modern Mandarin dì and Cantonese dai6; Middle Chinese dejH for 第; Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese *diːls for 第; and Baxter–Sagart (2014) *[l]ˤəjʔ-s. It analyzes 竹 as semantic and 弟 as phonetic, while noting the alternative that 第 may originally have been written 弟. This is a secondary reference, not independent paleographic proof.
evidence.title: 第 - Wiktionary

evidence.field: Old Chinese and Middle Chinese readings; pronunciation
evidence.text: The entry reports modern Mandarin dì and Cantonese dai6 for 弟 in the younger-brother reading; Middle Chinese dejX and Baxter–Sagart (2014) *lˤəjʔ; Zhengzhang (2003) gives *diːlʔ for that reading and also lists *diːls for a separate reading. Compared with 第, these systems show a shared sound base with differences in final/tone marking. Reconstructions are system-dependent, not direct recordings.
evidence.title: 弟 - Wiktionary

evidence.field: 讀音; 音韻方言
evidence.text: The entry gives 第 Mandarin dì, Cantonese dai6 and Guangyun 特計切, with Middle Chinese described as 定母霽韻去聲. Its 弟 entry gives both 徒禮切 and 特計切 readings. The corresponding departing-tone reading supports a phonetic comparison without establishing the earliest referent depicted by 弟.
evidence.title: 第 dì - 汉典

evidence.field: 說文解字; 音韻方言
evidence.text: The entry reports 弟's modern dì reading and quotes the Shuowen explanation 韦束之次弟也, interpreted by Duan Yucai as sequential bindings with leather. This is a historical lexicographic interpretation of the graphic form; the inspected evidence does not independently identify the depicted object or recover its original name and pronunciation.
evidence.title: 弟 dì - 汉典

evidence.text: The guide states that glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the query interface are released under CC0 1.0. This notice does not establish rights to other linked dictionary text or other Academia Sinica sites.

gaps: No inspected source provided visually inspected oracle-bone, bronze, Chu, Qin or seal glyphs for 第 with an argument identifying their parts; graphic chronology, component emergence and any possible corruption therefore remain unverified here.

The sourced Shuowen/MOE analysis is 竹 plus 弟, with 弟 described as a component, but the inspected text does not explicitly characterize 弟 as phonetic. Contemporary sources in the dossier assert a phonetic role, yet independent external confirmation with matched reconstructions for both 第 and 弟 was not obtained in this search.

No source in this session established an earlier graph 第 as bamboo strips arranged in sequence; the bamboo-writing rationale appears as a modern explanation in the dossier and a claim in the cited 《釋名》 note, not independently verified paleographic evidence.

The claim that the word was originally represented by 弟 and later differentiated with 竹 is reported in dictionary commentary, but no dated manuscript evidence was inspected to establish when the differentiated form arose or whether that was the actual graphic history. Origin_relation for 弟 should consequently be uncertain if treating it as a distinct origin form; component shape alone does not establish ancestry.

The reported 《小爾雅》 gloss “第，次也” was not independently checked against a primary text or dated witness; the exact earliest attestation of the sequence sense remains unestablished. The dictionary-cited Han, Tang and later examples are not a complete chronology.

Rank/order, evaluation, examination success, residence, and adverbial ‘only/just’ are separately evidenced as dictionary-recorded uses, but the semantic links among them and their dates of first occurrence are not fully established. The residence interpretation as a house graded by rank is a Kangxi-cited explanation, not independently proven here.

The dossier's phonological entries give conflicting Old Chinese forms from different systems (Zhengzhang *diːls versus Baxter-Sagart *[l]ˤəjʔ-s); this research did not locate primary system-specific entries for both 第 and 弟 and cannot resolve the differences or assert exact phonetic correspondence.

No external evidence was found in the inspected sources for the dossier claims that 第 contracts 第二/第一 in particular languages, or that it derives from 是 or 然; these appear to concern separate language-specific uses and remain unverified here.
No evidence in this research established the alleged relation to 梯 (‘ladder’), or validated Japanese kun readings as evidence of an origin; no Japanese-origin claim is supported.
The ctext attempt failed with 403 Forbidden. The CUHK database home page was inspected, but its 第-specific entry was not reached.

No inspected page supplied visually inspectable early 第 glyphs with a supported component-by-component argument. The indexed oracle, bronze, Chu, Qin, seal and clerical stages therefore do not establish a graphic sequence, component addition, specific corruption, or the date of a distinct 第 form.

The received-form analysis is 竹 plus 弟; the bamboo component is traditionally explained in connection with bamboo writing materials, but the early form evidence inspected here does not establish that rationale as the graph's original motivation.

Duan Yucai and Kangxi-era accounts report that 第 was originally 弟 or a shortened/common form of 弟. No dated manuscript evidence examined here establishes the chronology or the exact graphic change. The possibility of an earlier whole graph 弟 must remain a source-reported hypothesis.

弟 functions as a plausible phonetic component within 第: modern Mandarin readings are both dì, Cantonese readings are both dai6, and the cited reconstruction systems give related forms. Zhengzhang (2003) has 第 *diːls and 弟 *diːls for one reading; Baxter–Sagart (2014) has 第 *[l]ˤəjʔ-s versus 弟 *lˤəjʔ in the younger-brother reading. These are system-specific reconstructions with a final/tone difference. The earliest depicted referent and original spoken name for 弟 are not independently recovered here; that uncertainty does not itself invalidate its later phonetic role.

The exact earliest attestation of 第 with the sequence sense is unsettled. ZDIC attributes 第，次也 to 《小爾雅》, whereas the inspected transcription has 弟，次也. Neither the text's composition date nor the witness history was established in this session.

The Left Commentary passage uses 第 in an event narrated under Duke Ai's sixteenth year, but the passage's narrative date is not the date of its surviving textual witness and does not establish the character's first attestation.

Ranking/evaluating is supported by a Han Shu textual example; examination success by Bai Juyi's 815 text. Dictionary sources report residence and ‘only/just’ examples, but the earliest occurrence and semantic path for these uses were not established. Modern 第+numeral ordinal use must not be projected onto a first-attestation chronology from a dictionary gloss list.

The proposed connection to 梯 (‘ladder’), claims that 第 contracts language-specific words for ‘second’ or ‘first’, and claims connecting it with 是 or 然 were not corroborated by the inspected external sources. No Japanese-origin claim is supported.

The ctext page attempt returned 403; the CUHK site was inspected only at its home page; the Xiaoxuetang interface did not verify a 第-specific record. Commons lists candidate filenames, but the individual file pages could not be accessed, so no image met the identity and reuse-provenance threshold.
